Whole-brain mapping of inputs and outputs of four basal forebrain cell types in mice (cholinergic, glutamatergic, PV+ GABAergic, SOM+ GABAergic); inputs are largely shared across classes while outputs diverge widely, with glutamatergic and SOM+ neurons exhibiting greater reciprocal regional connectivity.

High-resolution ex vivo diffusion tractography and 7T fMRI in humans identify an ascending arousal network linking brainstem tegmental nodes, VTA, hypothalamus, thalamus, and basal forebrain with the default mode network to sustain wakefulness and conscious awareness.

Resting-state functional connectivity in humans reveals distinct cortical coupling profiles for anterior-medial (medial septum/diagonal band) versus posterior-lateral (nucleus basalis of Meynert) basal forebrain territories, demonstrating human corticotopic organization.

Ventral pallidal cholinergic neurons exhibit bursting firing, project selectively to BLA, mPFC, lateral habenula, and parasubthalamic nucleus, receive inputs from NAc, central amygdala, BNST, and VTA, and phasically signal rewards and punishments.

Cholinergic projection from anterior-medial basal forebrain (horizontal and vertical diagonal band) to prelimbic cortex (PrL); chemogenetic activation of this pathway enhances optimal response execution in a cued action-sequence task in mice.

Striatal D1 and D2 medium spiny neurons in nucleus accumbens differentially regulate substantia innominata cholinergic output to the basolateral amygdala (BLA): D1-MSNs disinhibit SI cholinergic neurons to drive BLA acetylcholine release during salient cue learning, while D2-MSNs suppress release.

Comprehensive anatomical synthesis of rat lateral septum (dorsal, intermediate, and ventral subdivisions): shows topographical hippocampal CA3/CA1 inputs and descending outputs to medial septum, preoptic area, lateral hypothalamus, mammillary bodies, and VTA.

Reviews comparative layer-specific cholinergic modulation of cortical microcircuits in rodents, monkeys, and humans; demonstrates differential nicotinic and muscarinic actions on layer 1 interneurons, layer 2/3 pyramidal cells, and deep infragranular projection neurons.

Compares basal forebrain cholinergic organization across species: highlights cortical afferents from OFC, PFC, and insula into NB/SI, subcortical inputs from amygdala and hypothalamus, and species-specific differences in cortical target innervation density.

Neuropeptide signaling in Drosophila operates across multiple organizational tiers—from local presynaptic gain control (sNPF, Tachykinin) to context-specific routing (Leucokinin, AstA) and organism-wide behavioral state coordination (SIFamide, DSK, DILPs, AKH, PDF) (fly).

A chemoconnectomic map across neurotransmitters, biogenic amines (5-HT, tyramine, octopamine, histamine), purinergic signals (AdoR), and over 40 neuropeptides establishes that chemical transmission extends beyond classical synaptic connectomes and underscores that neuronal activation is distinct from ligand deletion (fly).

Nitric oxide acts as an atypical diffusible cotransmitter in a subset of mushroom body dopaminergic neurons (PPL1-γ1pedc and PAM-γ5), activating soluble guanylate cyclase (Gyc88E) in Kenyon cells to generate slow cGMP signals that regulate memory decay and updating in functional opposition to rapid dopamine-driven reinforcement (fly).

Starvation upregulates short neuropeptide F receptor (sNPFR1) in Or42b olfactory receptor neurons; local sNPF release directly facilitates presynaptic transmitter release onto projection neurons to increase odor sensitivity during food search, independent of systemic NPF (fly).

Pigment-dispersing factor (PDF) released by ventrolateral clock pacemaker neurons (s-LNvs and l-LNvs) synchronizes central circadian oscillation, drives morning locomotor anticipation, and signals via PDF receptor (PDFR) to central complex ring neurons (fly).

Four SIFamide-expressing hub neurons in the pars intercerebralis project throughout the adult brain, translating hunger state into behavioral choices by suppressing courtship and promoting feeding through SIFaR-expressing target circuits (fly).

Heme oxygenase (HO) in Kenyon cells produces carbon monoxide (CO), which acts as a noncanonical retrograde messenger to regulate on-demand dopamine release and associative olfactory memory formation (fly).

Tyramine is not merely a precursor for octopamine synthesized by tyrosine decarboxylase (Tdc2); it acts via specific tyramine receptors (TyrR) to exert distinct, often antagonistic motor and behavioral effects, establishing that Tdc2-positive neurons cannot be assumed to be purely octopaminergic (fly).

Histamine synthesized by histidine decarboxylase (Hdc) in photoreceptors mediates fast inhibitory synaptic transmission to lamina monopolar neurons via the histamine-gated chloride channel ort (hclA/HisCl2) (fly).

Aggressive behavior in fruit flies is orchestrated by a combinatorial web of biogenic amines (serotonin, dopamine, octopamine) and neuropeptides (Tachykinin, DSK, NPF), demonstrating that neuromodulatory state biases action selection rather than mapping single chemicals to single behaviors (fly).

manual.title: Long-range neural pathways for octopus chemotactile processing revealed by whole-body microCT and functional tracing

finding: Whole-body microCT imaging (Octo9) of hatchling Octopus bimaculoides delineates continuous chemotactile trajectories from sucker chemotactile receptors and ganglia through axial arm nerve cords into the central brachial and inferior frontal lobes (octopus).

manual.title: Macroscale Connectivity in the Octopus Brain

finding: Reconstructs a directed, binary 32-region anatomical connectome of the octopus brain from classical and modern histological tracing, revealing small-world properties and modular organization across cognitive, visual and motor masses (octopus).
Subsecond acetylcholine transients in prelimbic cortex time cue detection in sustained attention tasks; optogenetic cholinergic activation improves attentional accuracy.
Optogenetically identified basal forebrain cholinergic neurons fire fast, millisecond-precision bursts to both unpredicted rewards and punishments, broadcasting a rapid reinforcement salience signal.

Synthesizes the attentional functions of cortical cholinergic inputs, detailing how nicotinic and muscarinic receptors optimize signal detection by filtering bottom-up inputs versus top-down cognitive context.

Parvalbumin-positive GABAergic basal forebrain projection neurons directly innervate prefrontal interneurons to rhythmically synchronize cortical gamma oscillations (30–80 Hz) and enhance perceptual sensitivity.

Traces dense, topographically organized descending projections from prefrontal (prelimbic, infralimbic, anterior cingulate) cortex directly to the substantia innominata/nucleus basalis complex in the rat.
Maps reciprocal topographically organized connections between the vertical limb of the diagonal band of Broca and medial prefrontal cortical areas.

Demonstrates that GABAergic medial septal projection neurons selectively innervate inhibitory interneurons in the hippocampus, establishing the anatomical substrate for the hippocampal theta rhythm pacemaker.

Reviews the physiology and network dynamics of hippocampal theta oscillations, detailing how the medial septum acts as the primary pacemaker pacing theta frequency and phase-locking pyramidal cell firing.

Reviews cholinergic modulation of hippocampal memory dynamics, detailing how acetylcholine selectively suppresses recurrent CA3 collaterals to prevent interference while enhancing entorhinal afferents during encoding.
Medial septal Vglut2+ glutamatergic projection neurons regulate locomotion speed-correlated theta frequency and firing rates of hippocampal pyramidal neurons.

Comprehensive monograph establishing the organization of rat lateral septal connections, including hippocampal CA1/subicular afferents and descending projections to medial septum, hypothalamus, and VTA.
Demonstrates direct catecholaminergic (dopaminergic and noradrenergic) synaptic innervation of basal forebrain cholinergic neurons in the rat.
Reviews locus coeruleus-noradrenergic modulation of behavioral state, demonstrating dense noradrenergic excitation of basal forebrain cholinergic neurons promoting cortical arousal.
Shows distinct reward-biased spatial representations in the lateral septum compared to dorsal hippocampus during goal-directed navigation.
Review: ADHD is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental disorder with genetic and environmental contributions, and its symptoms involve attention, impulsivity and hyperactivity across development.
Review: ADHD models include altered executive control, reward processing, arousal and developmental trajectories, with no single model explaining all cases.
Review: Contemporary ADHD neurobiology is limited by heterogeneity, small and confounded studies, and uncertain translation from group-level neural findings to individual mechanisms.

Review: Stimulant pharmacodynamics involve coordinated effects on catecholamine transporters and distributed brain networks, while the relationship between acute drug effects and ADHD pathophysiology remains unresolved.
Meta-analysis of 319 studies: ADHD groups showed greater reaction-time variability than typically developing groups, with smaller differences against clinical comparison groups and in adults.
Meta-analysis: ADHD was associated with steeper monetary delay discounting, although effect sizes varied with task and sample characteristics.

Molecular-imaging study: Adults with ADHD showed lower dopamine-related synaptic markers in reward-pathway regions than controls, supporting investigation of dopamine-related motivation without directly measuring dopamine concentration.

Mega-analysis of 1,713 ADHD participants and 1,529 controls found small average volume differences in the accumbens, amygdala, caudate, hippocampus and putamen, with larger differences in children than adults.
Coordinated analysis found subtle cortical surface-area differences in children with ADHD, while comparable case-control differences were not detected in adolescent or adult groups.

In nonhuman primate prefrontal cortex, moderate D1-receptor stimulation improved delay-related neuronal firing and working-memory performance, whereas excessive stimulation impaired them; related α2-adrenergic effects were observed with methylphenidate and atomoxetine.
Review: Guanfacine engages postsynaptic α2A-adrenoceptors in prefrontal cortex, reducing cAMP-related signaling and strengthening recurrent network interactions that support working memory.

Meta-analysis of magnetic-resonance-spectroscopy studies found higher glutamate-plus-glutamine concentrations in right medial prefrontal cortex in children with ADHD, with substantial methodological and regional heterogeneity.

Genome-wide analysis of 38,691 people with ADHD and 186,843 controls identified 27 risk loci and implicated genes expressed during early brain development, including enrichment in neuronal populations.
Meta-analysis found substantial heterogeneity in the EEG theta/beta ratio literature, with declining case-control differences across publication years, limiting its use as a universal ADHD biomarker.

Meta-analysis of 52 articles found ADHD-related differences in several cognitive event-related potentials, including P300, contingent negative variation and error positivity, with heterogeneous effects.

Longitudinal MTA data showed that ADHD symptom remission and recurrence varied across repeated assessments, supporting fluctuating developmental courses rather than a simple persistent-versus-remitted split.
